correctness.rationale: Every site-subset state with k vacancies admits pair intensity binom(k,2) and triple intensity λ binom(k,3); conditioning on the next accepted event yields u_k=[3/(3+λ(k-2))]u_(k-2)+[λ(k-2)/(3+λ(k-2))]u_(k-3), with u_0=0,u_1=1,u_2=0. The three-consecutive-coordinate stochastic transfer matrices have three-step products whose pairwise row overlap is at least min(q_j,q_(j+1),q_(j+2))/2 once q≤1/2. The harmonic divergent sum of q_k gives Dobrushin contraction and a common full-sequence limit, not just a subsequence limit. Exact coefficient summation yields λ z(1-z³)Fʹ+(3-2λ-3z²-λz³)F=(3-λ)z. The integrating factor z^(3/λ-2)(1-z³)e^(-3K(z)/λ), after subtracting z^a, gives an integrable lower-end regularization for a=3/λ-1>-1. Abel convergence evaluates the limit; λ=3 produces the closed form. Dominated convergence (α→0) and one-sided Laplace asymptotics (α→∞, φʹ(1)=2/3) establish endpoint-rate limits. Independent exact-rational checks verified 796 generating-equation coefficient cases and the transfer product; finite numerics are corroboration only.

value.rationale: Terminal Bernoulli jamming count on a completely interacting mixed-species substrate is a motivated exact observable; the full analytic rate-dependent law, elementary λ=3 value and disappearance of parity/mod-three size memory at every fixed positive minority rate describe genuine structural effects. An entire infinite substrate-size limit is proved analytically, not inferred from a few enumerated sizes. Scope is an idealized complete hypergraph and does not claim physical Euclidean adsorption predictions.

final_claim: For each fixed trimer-attempt rate λ>0 on the complete 2-/3-uniform hypergraph with per-edge pair rate 1, U_n converges to Bernoulli(L_λ), L_λ=e^(3K(1)/λ)[1+(3/λ-1)∫_0^1 t^(3/λ-2)(e^(-3K(t)/λ)-1)dt]/3, K(t)=∫_0^t s/(1+s+s²)ds. L_3=3^(-1/2)exp(-π/(6√3)); λ→0+ and λ→∞ limits are 1/2 and 1/3, respectively, but at λ=0 the parity law oscillates.
limitations: Complete two-/three-uniform hypergraph and fixed λ>0 only; not spatial 1D RSA.
Final vacancy law only, not adsorption times or accepted mixture counts.
No double-scaling λ=λ_n or sharp finite-size convergence exponent.
